questions.text: Under the EU rules on digital operational resilience of the financial sector, how often do the larger financial entities have to run advanced testing that simulates real attackers?
questions.gold: At least every three years (threat-led penetration testing, TLPT); the competent authority may ask for a lower or higher frequency. DORA Art. 26(1), dora.pdf p. 46.
probe: Häufigkeit erweiterter Tests anhand von TLPT

questions.text: In ENISA's threat landscape report for 2024, which share of the analysed incidents concerned threats against data (breaches, leaks)?
questions.gold: 19.01 % (about 1.91 K incidents), third after DoS/DDoS/RDoS (41.1 %) and ransomware (25.79 %). Only in the chart Figure 2, enisa-tl-2024.pdf p. 10 (printed page 9).

questions.text: An incident at a bank affects personal data, a high-risk AI system and the bank's ICT at the same time. What deadlines for reporting to the authorities do the GDPR, the AI Act and DORA each set?
questions.gold: GDPR: without undue delay, where feasible within 72 hours (Art. 33(1), dsgvo.pdf p. 52). AI Act: immediately after establishing the causal link, at the latest 15 days; 2 days for a widespread infringement or critical infrastructure; 10 days in case of death (Art. 73(2)-(4), ai-act.pdf p. 101-102). DORA: no fixed hours in the regulation - initial, intermediate and final report within time limits set by technical standards (Art. 19(4), 20(a)(ii), dora.pdf p. 42-43).

questions.text: For how long must the provider of a high-risk AI system keep its technical documentation available for the national authorities?
questions.gold: Ten years after the system was placed on the market or put into service (AI Act Art. 18(1), ai-act.pdf p. 63).
